explanation: Adding two matrices just means adding the numbers that sit in the SAME position, one cell at a time, so A and B must have the same shape. Scalar multiplication is even simpler: multiply EVERY entry by the same number s. The demo alternates between the two operations; the a and b sliders move the top-left entries so you watch one cell's result change, and the s slider rescales the whole matrix.
bullets: Add matrices position-by-position: (A+B)ij = aij + bij (same shape required).
Scalar multiply touches every entry: (s*A)ij = s * aij.
Both keep the matrix's shape; only the numbers inside change.
